jobs.title: Sr Program Manager, Metrology
jobs.description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

The Reliability team at Relativity Space ensures quality is built into every stage of the Terran R design and production process, embedding reliability from the very beginning. The team works directly with design, manufacturing, test, and launch teams to stay close to the hardware, understand constraints, and proactively shape decisions. As the program moves from development into production and scaled operations, this is the time to establish the right processes, controls, and inspections without slowing progress. The team plays a key role in balancing risk, fostering a culture of ownership, and making sure speed never comes at the cost of reliability. Success means creating a quality system that scales with the Terran R program and Relativity as a whole.

About the Role:

- Manage all internal and external calibrations of electrical, mechanical, optical, and RF measurement equipment, and oversee calibration of precision test equipment using NIST-traceable standards

- Drive multidisciplinary teams including metrology technicians, quality engineers, and operations personnel

- Define the long-term calibration strategy and roadmap, including evaluation of bringing calibration capabilities in-house

- Ensure vendors maintain compliance with ISO/IEC 17025, ANSI/NCSL Z540.3, AS9100, and NASA requirements

- Provide expert technical guidance on metrology and calibration, ensuring integrity and accuracy of measurement data used for critical decision-making

- Review calibration certificates and technical documentation, and maintain equipment tracking systems and calibration databases (e.g., Indysoft)

About You:

- 3-5+ years of progressive experience in metrology and calibration, with at least 1-2+ years in a program or project management role, preferably within aerospace, defense, or precision manufacturing

- Deep technical knowledge of calibration methods for electrical, mechanical, optical, and RF/microwave measurement equipment, dimensional metrology, and measurement uncertainty analysis and traceability principles

- Strong understanding of metrology standards including ISO/IEC 17025, ANSI/NCSL Z540.3, AS9100, and NIST traceability requirements

- Proficiency with multimeters, oscilloscopes, pressure/temperature gauges, dimensional tools, and calibration databases. Working with hardware/instrumentation exposed to process gases/fluids.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate complex technical information to expert and non-expert audiences

- Meticulous attention to detail and strong analytical skills

Nice to haves but not required:

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Physics, Metrology, or a closely related technical field (or equivalent experience with 7+ years in metrology/calibration)

- Experience establishing and scaling calibration programs from the ground up

- Self-starter with demonstrated ability to define and own processes and roll them out through effective communication to diverse teams

- Familiarity with blueprint and schematic interpretation

- ASQ Certified Calibration Technician (CCT) or equivalent certification

- Strong knowledge of enterprise applications (PLM, ERP, MES) and proficiency in data analysis tools

About the Team:

The Launch team operates at the intersection of every major aspect of Terran R, from stages and payloads to ground systems, launch, landing, and refurbishment. The Cape is the only place where you see it all come together, offering a level of exposure and responsibility unmatched elsewhere in the program. This is where first flights happen, where history is built on top of history, and where the scale of what's underway is unlike anything in modern aerospace. The mission stays the same, but the work evolves with every milestone: from first launch to reuse, high-cadence operations, and beyond. If you're looking to define what's next in space launch and write a new playbook, not just repeat what’s already been done, this is where it happens.

About the Role:

As a Staff Program Manager, Spaceport Integration, you will represent Relativity in coordination with external regulatory, government, and operational stakeholders. You will support compliance with applicable licenses, regulations, agreements, and operating procedures associated with spaceport and launch operations, including coordination with organizations such as the U.S. Space Force (USSF), NASA, and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

You will coordinate with internal engineering and operations teams and external stakeholders on activities supporting launch vehicle operations, facility development, hazardous operations, regulatory approvals, and mission readiness. This role provides exposure to a broad range of engineering and operational activities, including launch vehicle integration, launch operations, control room operations, civil infrastructure development, telemetry asset coordination, and local permitting.

- Serve as a primary point of contact for range-related operations and compliance activities, coordinating tasking between internal engineering teams and external stakeholders.

- Maintain documentation and coordinate activities required to support operational and regulatory compliance.

- Represent Relativity in meetings and coordination activities with the U.S. Space Force, NASA, state agencies, the U.S. Coast Guard, and other applicable regulatory or government organizations.

- Coordinate financial and contractual obligations between Relativity and applicable government stakeholders, including tracking funding requirements and supporting appropriate allocation of resources.

- Develop and implement processes that support design compliance, operational readiness, and reliable, high-cadence launch operations.

- Evaluate and improve organizational policies, systems, and processes, including opportunities to leverage automation and artificial intelligence.

- Participate in mission readiness activities, test article countdown operations, console operations, and emergency or contingency response activities as assigned.

- Work extended hours, weekends, or other non-standard schedules when required to support critical mission operations.

- Travel approximately 25% of the time, with travel requirements varying based on business and operational needs.

About You:

- Bachelor's degree in science, engineering, or a related technical discipline.

- Experience supporting operator console activities in space, launch, test, or related mission operations.

- Experience supporting national security space programs or other regulated space operations.

- 7+ years of experience managing complex technical projects, programs, or operations.

- Ability to obtain and maintain any background screening or access authorization required to perform the position's assigned duties at applicable Space Force installations.

- Ability to communicate technical, operational, contractual, and regulatory information effectively in written and verbal formats, including presenting information to internal and external stakeholders.

- Experience coordinating with the U.S. Space Force, NASA, FAA, or other government or regulatory organizations.

- Experience supporting launch range operations, spaceport operations, or launch vehicle integration.

- Experience with regulatory licensing, permitting, or operational compliance activities.

- Experience developing or implementing automated processes or tools for technical or operational workflows.

Nice to haves but not required:

- Active U.S. government security clearance.

Successful candidates must clear a background check administered by the US government to obtain clearance for on-site work at our government partner location in Cape Canaveral, Florida.

About the Team:

Relativity Space pioneered large-scale additive manufacturing with our Terran 1 rocket, the largest 3D-printed object to fly. Now a distinct business unit within Relativity, Horizon Manufacturing Technologies is advancing next-generation manufacturing for aerospace and beyond. The team operates at the frontier of manufacturing innovation, where creativity meets capability. This is an environment where cutting-edge R&D is put into production, industrializing advanced manufacturing capabilities to solve customer problems. You’ll work alongside welders, robotics engineers, data scientists, and systems engineers at the intersection of hardware and software, creating an end-to-end additive manufacturing platform that serves a wide variety of applications. From exploring new materials to unlocking faster print speeds, to designing complex, organic geometries that can’t be built any other way, it’s high-impact work that sets the foundation for the future of advanced manufacturing.

About the Role:

We’re seeking a strategic Business Development Manager to accelerate revenue growth by identifying, cultivating, and closing opportunities with customers in the aerospace, defense, maritime, and energy sectors. This person will be responsible for building trusted relationships with key decision-makers, understanding complex technical requirements and positioning our manufacturing capabilities as the solution of choice for critical components.

- Own and execute go-to-market strategies for target verticals: aerospace, defense, maritime, and energy sectors

- Identify and qualify new business opportunities through market research, inbound/outbound outreach, networking, and events

- Develop deep understanding of customer needs, technical specifications, and procurement cycles to tailor compelling proposals

- Partner with technical teams to scope solutions and communicate value to both engineering and executive stakeholders

- Manage the sales pipeline from initial contact (RFI/RFQ/RFP) to contract close, including proposal development, pricing strategy and negotiation

- Track and report on sales activities, pipeline health and forecasted revenue

- Represent Relativity at trade shows, industry conferences and site visits

- Provide competitive insights to help shape product strategy and commercial priorities

About You:

- 5+ years of business development or technical sales experience in advanced manufacturing, industrial equipment, defense or energy sectors

- Proven track record of closing complex deals

- Strong familiarity with one or more of the following: additive manufacturing, machining, welding or industrial robotics

- Ability to navigate matrixed organizations and influence technical and procurement stakeholders

- Excellent communication and presentation skills

- US Citizenship required (due to ITAR restrictions)

- Ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance is a plus

Nice to haves but not required:

- Existing network in energy, oil and gas, aerospace primes, or submarine contractors

- Experience selling into government or DoD-related programs (FAR/DFARS familiarity is a bonus)

- Engineering background or technical acumen to engage in detailed solution discussions

About the Team:

The Supply Chain team turns design intent into executable reality, balancing lead time, cost, complexity, and manufacturability to ensure we can build and scale Terran R. On this team, you're not just placing orders; you're actively shaping the solution. With full ownership across raw materials, capital equipment, and services, the role requires both strategic thinking and day-to-day execution. As the company scales, supply chain becomes increasingly central, working closely with engineering, quality, manufacturing, and more to make decisions that work for today but also for tomorrow. This is a team for those who want to operate at the intersection of technical ambition and business execution, driving tangible progress to keep the Terran R program on track.

About the Role

As Senior Manager of Indirect Supply Chain, you will lead a team of procurement professionals and set the strategy for a large, complex indirect portfolio spanning targeted local commodities and cross-site categories. At the local level, your scope will include ground support infrastructure, construction, and metal structures and fabrication, among others. You will shape multi-year category and supplier strategies, drive transformation across systems and processes, and serve as the trusted indirect procurement partner to senior stakeholders across the business — delivering cost, quality, and service performance today while building capability for tomorrow.

- Lead, coach, and develop a team of procurement professionals (category managers, sourcing specialists), setting priorities, building capability, and creating a culture of accountability and collaboration

- Own a large, complex indirect portfolio, accountable for total cost, savings, supplier performance, and service across categories

- Define and execute multi-year category and supplier strategies that balance near-term savings with long-term resilience and scalability

- Lead high-value and complex sourcing initiatives and negotiations, setting negotiation strategy and securing favorable commercial, technical, and delivery outcomes

- Develop senior-level supplier relationships and manage strategic supplier performance and continuous improvement

- Partner with and influence senior stakeholders across Finance, Launch and Testing, Facilities, HR, Legal, and business units, and represent indirect procurement in cross-functional and financial planning

- Lead the team to achieve KPI targets and drive continuous improvement across cost, quality, and service

- Lead transformation of indirect procurement systems and processes (ERP, P2P/S2P, e-sourcing, contract lifecycle management) to increase automation and data-driven decision-making

- Drive supplier risk management, third-party risk, and business continuity strategies for critical indirect suppliers and services

- Champion sustainability, supplier diversity, compliance, and responsible sourcing across the indirect portfolio

- Serve as the organization’s subject-matter expert on contracting best practices, advising on commercial terms and risk

About You

- Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field

- 8+ years of procurement or supply chain experience, with a significant focus on indirect categories

- 4+ years of people leadership, including developing and mentoring high-performing teams and, ideally, other leaders

- Proven track record setting and executing category and supplier strategies across a large, complex indirect portfolio, with measurable savings

- Strong negotiation expertise, with demonstrated success securing favorable commercial, technical, and delivery outcomes on complex agreements

- Deep knowledge of procurement systems and processes (ERP, P2P/S2P, e-sourcing, contract lifecycle management; e.g., SAP, Oracle, Coupa, Ariba)

- Executive-level communication skills, with the ability to influence and align stakeholders across all levels of the organization

- Demonstrated ability to build, scale, and mentor high-performing teams in a fast-paced environment

- Proven experience managing and developing complex contracts, with strong legal and commercial acumen

- Experience sourcing construction, capital projects, ground support equipment/infrastructure, or engineered and fabricated goods

Nice to Haves

- Master’s degree or MBA

- Professional certification such as CPSM, CPSD, or CIPS

- Experience leading indirect procurement transformation, including sustainability and supplier diversity programs

- Experience in a complex manufacturing environment (aerospace, defense, automotive, or frontier technology)

- Familiarity with government contracting, ITAR/export controls.
